title: Job Application and CV / Ntughari na nkwupụta azuike
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka 'ana m nwere 25 afọ' ma ọ bụ 'ana m na-akwado na Tourism', mana na English, nke a na-eme ka ụzọ dịghị ndụ: anyị na-eme ka ụzọ 'to have' na nkwupụta ndoro ndoro dịka 'in' ma ọ bụ 'from'. Kpọmkwem na ị na-eme ka 'experience' (nwere ọtụtụ 'experiences' na ndoro ndoro ndoro). Kpọmkwem na ị na-eme ka nkwupụta adịbeghị n'ime nkwupụta, nke a na-eme ka nkwupụta dị n'elu nke nkwupụta. Jiri 'I work as' ma ọ bụ 'I am responsible for' n'ihi na 'I dedicate myself to' na-eme ka ọ dị mfe n'okpuru.
rule: Iji kwuo okwu gị na ntughari ndoro ndoro na English na B1: 1) Jiri 'present simple' iji kwuo okwu gị na ntughari ndoro ndoro: 'I work as a...' (Ana m na-eme ka...), 'I am responsible for...' (Ana m na-akwado na...). 2) Na ntughari ndoro ndoro na-agba, jiri 'used to' ma ọ bụ 'past simple': 'I used to work at...' / 'I worked at...'. 3) Nkwupụta 'have' na-eme ka ọ dị n'okpuru nwere ike ịnata afọ na ike: 'I have five years of experience' (Ana m nwere afọ ise n'ime ntughari). 4) Nkwupụta adịbeghị n'ime nkwupụta, nke a na-eme ka nkwupụta dị n'elu nke nkwupụta: 'I have strong communication skills' (ana m nwere ike ịnata okwu ndoro ndoro). 5) Jiri 'in' na ndoro ndoro ('experience in hospitality'), 'at' na ndoro ndoro ('at a hotel'), na 'as' na ndoro ndoro ('as a manager'). 6) Na nkwupụta azuike, anyị na-eme ka nkwupụta ndoro ndoro na-egosi na nkwupụta ndoro ndoro, nke a na-eme ka nkwupụta ndoro ndoro nwere ike ịnata.

concept_examples.text: I have five years of experience in customer service.
concept_examples.translation: Ana m nwere afọ ise n'ime ntughari na ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv faɪv jɪrz əv ɪkˈspɪriəns ɪn ˈkʌstəmər ˈsɜrvɪs/

concept_examples.text: I am responsible for managing the sales team.
concept_examples.translation: Ana m na-akwado na ịnata ndoro ndoro n'ime ụlọ ego.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm rɪˈspɑnsəbəl fər ˈmænɪdʒɪŋ ðə seɪlz tim/

concept_examples.text: She studied marketing at the university.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị n'ụlọ ọgbakọ, ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị n'ụlọ ọgbakọ.

concept_examples.text: I would like to apply for the position of cashier.
concept_examples.translation: Ana m na-achọ ịkpọpụta na ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tə əˈplaɪ fər ðə pəˈzɪʃən əv ˈkæʃɪr/

common_error.wrong: I have 30 years and I am graduated in marketing.
common_error.correct: I am 30 years old and I graduated in marketing.
common_error.correct_alt: I am 30 years old and I have a degree in marketing.
common_error.explanation: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka 'ana m nwere afọ 30' na 'ana m na-akwado na', mana na English, anyị na-eme ka nkwupụta 'to be' na afọ ('I am 30 years old') ma ọ bụghị 'am graduated' n'ihi na 'graduate' bụ nkwupụta ndoro ndoro ('I graduated'). Na ntughari, anyị na-eme ka 'have a degree in' (nwere ntughari na). Ọtụtụ mmadụ na-eme ka ọ dịghị 'old' n'ime afọ. Kpọmkwem: 'I am + number + years old' na 'graduate from' ma ọ bụ 'have a degree in'.

levels.label: Talking about Personal Information
levels.translation: Izu okwu gbasara okwukwe ndoro ndoro

examples.original: I am 28 years old.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈtweɪti eɪt jɪrz oʊld/
examples.translation: Ana m nwere afọ abụọ na anọ.
examples.note: Anyị na-eme ka 'am' na afọ, ma ọ bụghị 'have' dịka na Spanish.

examples.original: I was born in Mexico City.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wəz bɔrn ɪn ˈmɛksɪkoʊ ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: Ana m bịara na ụlọ ezi obodo Mexico.
examples.note: Jiri 'be born' na nkwupụta ndoro ndoro, ma ọ bụghị 'born' n'okpuru. 'In' na-eme ka ụlọ ezi obodo.

examples.original: I live in Valencia, Spain.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ lɪv ɪn vəˈlɛnsiə, speɪn/
examples.translation: Ana m na-eri na Valencia, Spain.

examples.original: I have a degree in business administration.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə dɪˈgri ɪn ˈbɪznəs ədˌmɪnɪˈstreɪʃən/

examples.note: 'Have a degree in' + ndoro ndoro. Jiri 'I am a graduate in'.

examples.original: I am proficient in English and Spanish.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm prəˈfɪʃənt ɪn ˈɪŋglɪʃ ənd ˈspænɪʃ/
examples.translation: Ana m nwere ike ndoro ndoro na English na Spanish.
examples.note: 'Proficient in' na-eme ka ọ dị mma. Jiri 'I am good in'.

examples.original: I studied computer science for four years.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈstʌdid kəmˈpjutər ˈsaɪəns fər fɔr jɪrz/
examples.translation: Ana m nwere ike nkwupụta na computer science na afọ anọ.

levels.label: Talking about Work Experience

examples.original: I worked as a sales assistant for two years.

examples.translation: Ana m na-eme ka ndoro ndoro na-eri na ụlọ ego na afọ abụọ.

examples.original: Currently, I am working at a hotel.
examples.phonetic: /ˈkɜrəntli, aɪ æm ˈwɜrkɪŋ æt ə hoʊˈtɛl/
examples.translation: Ezigbo, ana m na-eme ka ndoro ndoro na-eri na ụlọ ego.

examples.original: I am responsible for answering emails and managing bookings.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm rɪˈspɑnsəbəl fər ˈænsərɪŋ ˈimeɪlz ənd ˈmænɪdʒɪŋ ˈbʊkɪŋz/
examples.translation: Ana m na-akwado na ihe ndoro ndoro na-egosi na email na ntughari na-eri na ụlọ ego.

examples.original: I used to work in customer service.

examples.note: 'Used to' na-eme ka ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro na-agba.

title: Discussing current events / Maka ihe mere n'oge a
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka anyị na-akwado na nke mere n'oge a, na nke mere n'oge gara aga, na n'kpuru okwu dị ka 'na according to' ma 'dicen que'. Na Igbo, anyị na-akwado na nke mere n'oge a na nke mere n'oge gara aga, na nke mere n'oge gara aga. Na English, anyị na-akwado na nke mere n'oge a na nke mere n'oge gara aga, na nke mere n'oge gara aga. Na English, anyị na-akwado na nke mere n'oge a na nke mere n'oge gara aga, na nke mere n'oge gara aga. Na English, anyị na-akwado na nke mere n'oge a na nke mere n'oge gara aga.
rule: Iji kwuo maka ihe mere n'oge a na English na level B1: 1. Jiri 'present perfect' (have/has + participle) iji kwuo maka ihe mere n'oge a n'efu n'ime nke gara aga: 'Scientists have discovered a new planet.' 2. Jiri 'past simple' iji kwuo maka nkọwa n'ime nke gara aga: 'They announced the result yesterday.' 3. Jiri 'present continuous' iji kwuo maka ihe na-eme n'oge a: 'The government is debating the new law.' 4. Iji kwuo maka ike, jiri nkpuru okwu dị ka 'I think', 'In my opinion', 'I believe' na nke na-eme ka ọ bụrụ na ọ bụghị nke na-akwado nke mere n'oge a. 5. Nkọwa ndoro ndoro: 'headline', 'article', 'report', 'according to', 'latest', 'issue'.

concept_examples.text: The government has announced new measures to reduce pollution.
concept_examples.translation: The government has announced new measures to reduce pollution.
concept_examples.phonetic: ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt hæz əˈnaʊnst nuː ˈmɛʒərz tə rɪˈdjuːs pəˈluːʃən.

concept_examples.text: According to the news, the situation is improving slowly.
concept_examples.translation: According to the news, the situation is slowly improving.
concept_examples.phonetic: əˈkɔːrdɪŋ tə ðə nuːz, ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən ɪz ɪmˈpruːvɪŋ ˈsloʊli.

concept_examples.text: I think the article was very biased.
concept_examples.translation: I think the article was very biased.
concept_examples.phonetic: aɪ θɪŋk ði ˈɑːrtɪkl wəz ˈveri ˈbaɪəst.

concept_examples.text: Have you heard about the election results?
concept_examples.translation: Have you heard about the election results?
concept_examples.phonetic: hæv juː hɜːrd əˈbaʊt ði ɪˈlɛkʃən rɪˈzʌlts?

common_error.wrong: The government has announced new measures yesterday.
common_error.correct: The government announced new measures yesterday.
common_error.correct_alt: The government has announced new measures. (sin tiempo específico)
common_error.explanation: The error occurs because in Spanish, one can say 'ha anunciado ayer' in some regions, but in English, the present perfect is not combined with a specific time like 'yesterday'. Use the past simple for actions with a defined time. For 'yesterday', 'last week', etc., avoid 'have/has'.

examples.original: The economy is growing again.
examples.phonetic: ðə iˈkɒnəmi ɪz ˈɡroʊɪŋ əˈɡɛn.
examples.translation: The economy is growing again.
examples.note: Use the present continuous to describe a current trend.

examples.original: Scientists have found a new vaccine.
examples.phonetic: ˈsaɪəntɪsts hæv faʊnd ə nuː vækˈsiːn.
examples.translation: Scientists have found a new vaccine.
examples.note: The present perfect is used to announce something recent without an exact date.

examples.original: Conflict in the region has escalated.
examples.phonetic: ˈkɒnflɪkt ɪn ðə ˈriːdʒən hæz ˈɛskəleɪtɪd.
examples.translation: The conflict in the region has escalated.
examples.note: Observe the use of 'has' with a singular subject.

examples.original: The accident happened at 8 p.m. last night.
examples.phonetic: ði ˈæksɪdənt ˈhæpənd æt eɪt piː ɛm læst naɪt.
examples.translation: The accident occurred at 8 PM.
examples.note: The past simple is for specific facts at a particular time.

examples.original: Meanwhile, the prime minister was talking to reporters.
examples.phonetic: ˈmiːnwaɪl, ðə praɪm ˈmɪnɪstər wəz ˈtɔːkɪŋ tə rɪˈpɔːrtərz.
examples.translation: Meanwhile, the prime minister was speaking to journalists.
examples.note: The past continuous describes an action in progress in the past.

examples.original: In my opinion, the government should react quickly.
examples.phonetic: ɪn maɪ əˈpɪnjən, ðə ˈɡʌvərmənt ʃʊd riˈækt ˈkwɪkli.
examples.translation: In my opinion, the government should react quickly.
examples.note: Use 'should' to give recommendations.

examples.original: I can't believe they decided that!
examples.phonetic: aɪ kænt bɪˈliːv ðeɪ dɪˈsaɪdɪd ðæt!
examples.translation: I can't believe they decided that!
examples.note: Express surprise with 'can't believe' + past simple.

title: Cultural Differences and Misunderstandings / Ndoro ndoro dị na ndoro ọdịda
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-egosi ụzọ dị iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa, n'ihi na na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa, n'ihi na na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa, n'ihi na na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa. Ma ọ bụ na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa. Ma ọ bụ na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa. Ma ọ bụ na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa. Ma ọ bụ na English, ndị mmadụ na-egosi iche iche ma ọ bụ nkwụ ụzọ dị mkpa.
rule: Iji kwuo ndoro ndoro dị na ndoro ọdịda na English na B1, ọ dị mkpa ịnụ ya: 1) Ndoro ndoro ndoro: 'Could you explain that?' n'ime 'Explain that'. 2) Ndoro ndoro ndoro: 'I think', 'I feel', 'I guess' iji mee ma ọ bụghị dị mkpa. 3) Ndoro ndoro ndoro: 'Do you mean...?', 'Are you saying...?' iji nweta ndoro ndoro. 4) Iji were simple past na ndoro ndoro: 'I misunderstood' (ghị 'I have misunderstood' ma ọ bụghị n'ime na ụbọchị ndoro). Gịnị ka ị na-egosi 'tener razón' (to be right, ghị 'to have reason') ma ọ bụ 'hacer falta' (to need, ghị 'to make lack').

concept_examples.text: I thought you were coming at 7, but you came at 8.
concept_examples.translation: Mụtara na ị ga-abịa na 7, mana ị banye na 8.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ θɔːt juː wɜːr ˈkʌmɪŋ æt ˈsɛvn bʌt juː keɪm æt eɪt/

concept_examples.text: Could you repeat that? I didn't understand.
concept_examples.translation: Ị ga-eme ka ị were ya n'ụzọ ọma? Mụnwere ike ịghọta.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː rɪˈpiːt ðæt aɪ ˈdɪdnt ˌʌndərˈstænd/

concept_examples.text: In my culture, it's polite to take off your shoes.
concept_examples.translation: Na mụnụ ndoro anyị, ọ dị mma ịgọọ akwụ ụkwọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ ˈkʌltʃər ɪts pəˈlaɪt tə teɪk ɒf jɔːr ʃuːz/

concept_examples.text: He said he'd call, but he didn't.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ gwara na ọ ga-eme ka ọ bụrụ na ọ dịghị.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː sɛd hiːd kɔːl bʌt hiː ˈdɪdnt/

common_error.wrong: You have reason, but I think different.
common_error.correct: You're right, but I think differently.
common_error.correct_alt: You may be right, but I see it differently.
common_error.explanation: Ọ bụ n'ihi na na Spanish, anyị na-egosi 'tener razón' (na-agụ 'to have reason') ma ọ bụ 'pensar diferente' (ghị adverb nke 'differently'). Na English, anyị na-egosi 'to be right' (ghị 'to have reason') ma ọ bụ adverb 'differently' (ghị adjective 'different'). Iji were ya, chọpụta na 'reason' bụ noun nke na-egosi 'motive', ghị 'reason' n'ime usoro ịbịa n'ọnọdụ ịbịa.

examples.original: I think that's a good idea.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ θɪŋk ðæts ə gʊd aɪˈdɪə/
examples.translation: Mụtara na ọ dị mma.
examples.note: Jiri 'I think' n'ime 'I believe' iji were ndoro ndoro na mkparịta ụka.

examples.original: Maybe we could try another way.
examples.phonetic: /ˈmeɪbi wiː kʊd traɪ əˈnʌðər weɪ/
examples.translation: Ọ ga-eme ka anyị were ụzọ ọzọ.
examples.note: 'Maybe' na-eme mkpa, na-akpali na 'quizás' na Spanish.

examples.original: I'm not sure that's true.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm nɒt ʃʊə ðæts truː/
examples.translation: A na-eme m nkwụ ụzọ na ọ bụghị ọnọdụ ndoro.
examples.note: Na English, anyị na-egosi 'not sure' iji kwuo ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụghị n'ime.

examples.original: What do you mean by that?
examples.phonetic: /wɒt duː juː miːn baɪ ðæt/
examples.translation: Gịnị ka ị na-egosi na ndoro a?
examples.note: Ndoro a bụ ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụghị n'ime, ọ bụghị 'What?' nke na-eme mkpa.

examples.original: Could you explain that more slowly?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː ɪkˈspleɪn ðæt mɔːr ˈsloʊli/
examples.translation: Ị ga-eme ka ị were ya n'ụzọ ọma?
examples.note: 'Could' bụ ndoro ndoro ndoro nke na-eme mkpa n'ime 'can' iji were ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: Do you mean the meeting is tomorrow?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː miːn ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ ɪz təˈmɒroʊ/
examples.translation: Ị na-egosi na ndoro a ga-abịa na ụbọchị?
examples.note: Jiri 'Do you mean...?' iji nweta ndoro ndoro.

levels.label: Describing Cultural Differences
levels.translation: Describiendo ndoro ndoro dị na ndoro ọdịda

examples.original: In Spain, people eat lunch late.

examples.translation: Na Spain, ndị mmadụ na-egosi ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro
examples.note: Aprende a usar 'in + país' para hablar de costumbres.

examples.original: That's very different from my culture.
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ˈvɛri ˈdɪfərənt frɒm maɪ ˈkʌltʃər/
examples.translation: Eso es muy diferente de mi cultura.

examples.original: We never do that in my country.
